cse-2017-2-cs-23.approach: Use the handshake lemma: the degree sum is twice the edge count, and every vertex contributes at least 3, which caps $n$. Then check the bound is achievable.

steps.title: Degree sum
steps.body: $\sum \deg(v) = 2|E| = 2 \times 25 = 50$.

steps.title: Lower bound per vertex
steps.body: Each vertex has degree $\ge 3$, so $3n \le 50 \Rightarrow n \le \frac{50}{3} = 16.67 \Rightarrow n \le 16$.

steps.title: Achievability
steps.body: With $n = 16$: take 14 vertices of degree 3 and 2 of degree 4, sum $= 14 \times 3 + 2 \times 4 = 42 + 8 = 50$. Such a simple graph exists (e.g. a 3-regular graph on 16 vertices has 24 edges; add one edge between two non-adjacent vertices). So the maximum is $16$.

pitfalls: Rounding $50/3$ up to 17 — then the degree sum would need at least $51 > 50$.
cse-2017-2-cs-23.verification: A 3-regular graph on 16 vertices has $16 \cdot 3 / 2 = 24$ edges; one extra edge gives 25 edges with all degrees $\ge 3$.

cse-2017-2-cs-24.approach: Read the coefficients 13 and 36 as base-$b$ numerals and use Vieta's formulas (sum and product of roots) with the roots 5 and 6.

steps.title: Convert coefficients
steps.body: $(13)_b = b + 3$ and $(36)_b = 3b + 6$. The roots 5 and 6 are single digits, the same in any base $b > 6$.

steps.title: Sum of roots
steps.body: $5 + 6 = 11 = b + 3 \Rightarrow b = 8$.

pitfalls: Treating 13 and 36 as decimal — then the roots would be 4 and 9, not 5 and 6.
cse-2017-2-cs-24.verification: In base 8: $x^2 - 11x + 30 = (x-5)(x-6)$ in decimal, matching the given roots.

steps.title: Restate the language
steps.body: $L = \{ w : |w| \ge 6 \text{ and the 3rd symbol of } w \text{ is } a \}$.

steps.title: Count the prefix
steps.body: States $q_0, q_1, q_2$ count the first two symbols (any letter). On the 3rd symbol: $a \to q_3$, $b \to D$ (dead, since no extension can be accepted).

steps.title: Count the suffix
steps.body: After the $a$ we need at least 3 more symbols: $q_3 \to q_4 \to q_5 \to q_6$ on any symbol, and $q_6$ is accepting with a self-loop.

scene.caption: Three more symbols reach the accepting state

steps.title: All states distinct
steps.body: For $q_i$ ($0 \le i \le 6$) the shortest accepted continuation has a different length, and only $q_0, q_1, q_2$ care about a specific later symbol at a fixed position; $D$ accepts nothing. Hence all $7 + 1 = 8$ states are pairwise distinguishable.

steps.title: Joint probability
steps.body: $P(P \cap Q) = P(Q \mid P)\,P(P) = \frac13 \times \frac14 = \frac{1}{12}$.

steps.title: Probability of Q
steps.body: $P(Q) = \frac{P(P \cap Q)}{P(P \mid Q)} = \frac{1/12}{1/2} = \frac16$.

steps.title: Neither applies
steps.body: $P(P \cup Q) = \frac14 + \frac16 - \frac1{12} = \frac{3 + 2 - 1}{12} = \frac{4}{12} = \frac13$, so $P(\bar P \cap \bar Q) = 1 - \frac13 = \frac23$.

steps.title: Condition on not Q
steps.body: $P(\bar P \mid \bar Q) = \frac{2/3}{1 - 1/6} = \frac{2/3}{5/6} = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{6}{5} = \frac45$.

$\frac56$ is $P(\bar Q)$, the denominator, not the conditional probability.

steps.title: Check (A)
steps.body: $wx + wx + wy + x + xy = wx + wy + x = x + wy$ (absorption $x + wx = x$) ✓.

steps.title: Check (B)

steps.title: Check (D)
steps.body: $(w + y)(wxy + wyz) = wxy + wyz + wxy + wyz = wxy + wyz$ ✓ (since $ww = w$, $yy = y$). So (C) is INCORRECT.

steps.body:
Need $r_2(Y), w_2(Y)$ before $r_1(Y)$. Let $k \ge 2$ be the number of $T_2$ ops before $r_1(Y)$. Before it: $r_1(X), w_1(X)$ and $k$ ops of $T_2$ → $\binom{k+2}{2}$ ways; after it: $w_1(Y)$ and $4 - k$ ops of $T_2$ → $5 - k$ ways.

$k = 2$: $6 \times 3 = 18$; $k = 3$: $10 \times 2 = 20$; $k = 4$: $15 \times 1 = 15$. Total $= 18 + 20 + 15 = 53$.

steps.title: Total
steps.body: $53 + 1 = 54$ conflict-serializable schedules (out of $\binom84 = 70$).

pitfalls: Forgetting the serial schedule $T_1 T_2$.
Counting only the two serial schedules.
cse-2017-2-cs-44.verification: Complement: non-serializable schedules have $r_1(Y)$ before $w_2(Y)$ and $r_2(Y)$ before $w_1(Y)$; $70 - 54 = 16$ of them.
